messages.subject: Wrong night time detecting
parts:
Dear all,

I am new to using an accelerometer with R/GGIR, so i hope someone can help me.

I recorded a week with axivity and i tried to analyze csv file with GGIR  package, but from the summary report that you can see in attached, it seems that i sleep during the day. 
For example in day 2 it seems i sleep from 9.40 am to 5.40 pm instead of from midnight to 8 am.

Hope to get help from you.

Thank you so much.
Best
Luca

messages.author: e17dc21aa6c006ab
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Wrong night time detecting
parts:
Hi Luca, 

did you use sleeplog (Diary) to identify TimeInBed? If you entirely relied on the VanHess algorithm to identify TimeinBed there is little error expected. In my experience using a diary sleep log is more accurate. Moreover, it seems something went wrong in timestamp labeling since there is more acceleration in the night compared to the day. 

It's better to share your script as well, so someone can help better. 

Best Regards, 
Abdul Haleem

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Wrong night time detecting
parts:
Hi Luca and Abdul,

I don't think this is related to the accuracy of the algorithms. Sleep period time in the second day starts at noon because GGIR interprets this day as daysleeper and then the detection of the sleep period time starts at noon. What apparently is wrong here is the timestamps, which seems not to be in the correct timezone. Have you defined the argument desiredtz and configtz? If you are processing data that was collected in a different timezone, then it is relevant to set these arguments to correctly build up the timestamps.

Best,
Jairo
